Abdus Sattar Khondker and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.

full_judgment: 8. While arguing the case Mr Quayum did not refer to the case reported in 10 DLR 79 but when this case was brought to his notice, the learned Advocate tried to distinguish the aforesaid case on the ground that in that case the application under section 151 was made in a pending suit. I think that we may profitably refer to the decision reported in 10 DLR 79, wherein it has been held that an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure would lie seeking relief when the party alleging fraud was not a party to the order made by the court as a result of fraud practised upon the court. In that case it has been spelt out that when the allegation is that the decree was obtained by practising fraud on the court and the party complaining of fraud has been shown to be one of the parties to the solenama as agreeing to it, whereas he is completely ignorant about the solenama, the court has an inherent power, in fact, it is duty bound to set aside the solenama as an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. A case of this description is completely different from the class of cases where a person who is a party to a suit and assents to a consent decree which he subsequently seeks to impeach on the ground that his assent was obtained by fraud. In a case of this latter class, relief cannot be obtained by an application under section 151 of the Code, but a proper way of proceeding for setting aside the decree would be to institute a regular suit.
